clue.text: Spell inhaling pot leads to physical collapse

indicators.note: inhaling means the first piece takes the second into its middle, as lungs take in air

parts.note: a spell of activity is a bout
an urn is a pot or vase

explanation.surface: A stretch of smoking cannabis ends with someone keeling over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks like magic but is a period of time; 'pot' looks like cannabis but is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnout is the exhausted collapse that follows overwork, a physical and mental breakdown.

clue.text: Marc, say, has cereal daily to avoid trouble

parts.note: bran is the husk of cereal grain

indicators.note: to avoid means to keep away from, so the letters are removed

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A man called Marc has cereal every day to keep out of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marc' looks like a man's name, but it is the French spirit distilled from grape pressings.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a kind of brandy made from the skins and pips left after winemaking, an example.

clue.text: Not so placid, finding percentage of interest reduced by bank

indicators.note: reduced means made smaller, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a rate is the percentage charged as interest
a tier is a bank or row of seats

explanation.surface: Someone is upset that their interest rate has been cut by the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks financial, fitting 'interest', but is a row, TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattier means more irritable or bad-tempered, the comparative opposite of calm.

clue.text: Varnish here without delay

definitions.meaning: the place where nail varnish is painted, on a fingernail
promptly, as in payment made immediately

explanation.surface: Polish applied quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment on the nail means immediate payment; the literal reading is where nail polish goes.

clue.text: Academic put quote the wrong way round during the examination

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination, preceded by the

indicators.note: the wrong way round means read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A scholar misquoted something during a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way round' makes ETIC; 'the examination' is THE ORAL, a spoken exam, and 'put' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic in the sense of abstract and not practical means much the same as theoretical.

clue.text: Snatched forty winks during the day?

indicators.note: during means one thing happens inside the span of another, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Wed is the short form of Wednesday, a day
forty winks is a short nap or rest

explanation.surface: Someone grabbed a quick nap in the middle of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'day' is a particular day, abbreviated WED.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest something is to pull it away forcibly, so wrested is a synonym of grabbed.

clue.text: Rainy in one area (not South)

indicators.note: not South means that letter is excluded

parts.note: the West is one area of a country

explanation.surface: It is rainy in one region of the country, not the south.
explanation.walkthrough: The West of Britain is famously wetter than elsewhere, which fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet weather is rainy weather, a simple synonym.

clue.text: Brit abroad spoke at great length, being half-cut

indicators.note: half-cut means half the word is chopped off, keeping the first five letters

parts.note: to expatiate is to speak or write at length

explanation.surface: A Briton overseas talked on and on while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for tipsy, but here it means EXPATIATED loses its second half.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat is someone living outside their own country, such as a Briton settled overseas.

clue.text: One cruises in this, say, turning up in a port in a storm

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other
in a storm suggests tossed about, so the letters are scrambled
turning up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: eg means for example, signalled by say

explanation.surface: A ship cruises into harbour during a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a storm' makes TOPAR; 'cruises' suggests a ship, which the port supports, but the cruising is done by car.
explanation.definitionFit: Top gear is the highest gear of a car, used when cruising at speed.

clue.text: Small green salad finally served up with salmon, perhaps

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, reversed
finally picks the last letter

parts.note: green means raw or unripe
salmon is an example of a fish

explanation.surface: A green salad is served with salmon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns the pair round together to make DWAR; in a down clue up means read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwarfish means very small, like a dwarf.

clue.text: Article printed by newspaper about tax aimed against criminals

parts.note: an is the indefinite article in grammar
a tithe was a tax of a tenth paid to the church
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A grammar piece appears beside a newspaper story on taxation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'printed by' means set beside; 'about' is just a link, the paper being about the tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Antitheft devices such as alarms and locks are designed to thwart thieves and robbers.

clue.text: One takes part in piano trio by a woman

indicators.note: takes part in means joins the group, so the letter goes inside the trio

parts.note: p is the musical mark for piano, quiet, and a trio of them gives three
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A musician joins a piano trio alongside a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano trio' looks like a chamber ensemble but is three letters P.
explanation.definitionFit: Pippa is a female given name, so it stands for an unnamed woman.

clue.text: Motor I have taken on back road

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for road is read in reverse

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone has bought a car and taken it out onto a back road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back road' looks like a country lane, but 'back' is the reversal signal; 'taken on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To motor is to travel by car, the same verb as to drive.

clue.text: Before Sat, cooked part of lunch for Sun?

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients prepared and mixed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something prepared before Saturday forms part of the meal on Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' is short for Sunday, when the British traditionally eat a roast for lunch; it also hints at the tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint of roast beef is the classic centrepiece of the traditional British Sunday dinner.

clue.text: This is how people are crammed into a tiny ship, a cause of fear

indicators.note: are crammed into means packed inside, so the pieces go within the others

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
so means in this way
men means people
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Packing passengers into a little boat is frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This is how' is a phrase standing for a single word meaning thus; the inserted piece goes after the first two letters of the small ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Awesomeness is the quality of inspiring awe, a mixture of dread and wonder.

clue.text: Poorly rated thesp shortly about to go on and act

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go around the other piece
poorly means badly done, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: to board is to go on a ship, train or plane

explanation.surface: A badly reviewed actor is about to go on stage and perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' drops the last letter of the actor; 'Poorly' makes TREADTHES, and 'about' puts it round the boarding verb before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on stage is to appear in theatre, the idiom being to walk the stage planks.

clue.text: Funeral rites old boy attends, inhaling endless tobacco

indicators.note: inhaling means taking in, so the trimmed tobacco goes inside

parts.note: to see to something is to attend, so attends gives sees

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a quid is a chew of tobacco

explanation.surface: An old boy attends a funeral, breathing in tobacco smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter of the chew of tobacco; a quid is a plug of chewing tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsequies are funeral ceremonies or rites, a formal word.

clue.text: Notice a fellow has swallowed second drink

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement

indicators.note: has swallowed means contains, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: a male is a fellow, a man

explanation.surface: A man notices that a fellow drank a second drink.
explanation.walkthrough: ADAM'S ALE is a humorous term for water.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is jocular slang for water, the only drink Adam had.

clue.text: Selling return ferry tickets for this?

definitions.meaning: selling someone out is betraying them, deceitful treachery
a return ferry ticket buys a trip across water twice, there and back

explanation.surface: Someone sells return tickets for a ferry.
explanation.definitionFit: Double-crossing is betraying an ally, and a return ferry ticket gives two sea passages.

clue.text: Country under Britain's sound rule

indicators.note: under in a down clue means the second piece comes below the first

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom, Britain

indicators.note: sound means as heard, so the word is spelt by how it is said

parts.note: reign means rule

explanation.surface: A country lies beneath Britain's secure governance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like secure, but signals a homophone of REIGN, spelt RAINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is a country of Eastern Europe.

clue.text: Part of Hanoi, somewhere unpleasant

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A district of Vietnam's capital is a nasty place.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or disagreeable, especially of a smell.

clue.text: Don't move antique buffet around

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: to buffet is to hit
antique means old

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep still as an old sideboard is moved around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' looks like the furniture or meal but is the verb, to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Hold it is an instruction to stay still or freeze.

clue.text: In back room I found a dish for fruit

indicators.note: In means placed inside, so the letter sits within the reversed abbreviation
back means the abbreviation for room is read in reverse

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive woman, a belle

explanation.surface: In a back room someone finds a dish to put fruit in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' looks like crockery but is a beautiful woman, BELLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The mirabelle is a small yellow plum, a type of stone fruit.

clue.text: Bar lunches oddly enough for Aussie

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters are taken

explanation.surface: Bar meals are strangely sufficient for an Australian.
explanation.walkthrough: Bruce is a stereotypical Australian male name in British humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruce is a stock name for an Australian man, as in Monty Python's sketch.

clue.text: Desert round city in S America

parts.note: to desert is to quit or abandon
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A city in South America surrounded by desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Quito is the capital of Ecuador, high in the Andes of South America.

clue.text: A political organisation employs policeman for so long

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, a police officer
EU is the European Union, a political organisation

explanation.surface: A political body hires a police officer for a long stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like a stretch of time, but it is the farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for farewell, the same parting phrase as cheerio or goodbye.

clue.text: Wandering tribe assigned to area avoiding eastern Turkish port

indicators.note: wandering means roaming about, so the letters move around

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping clear of, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: zoned means assigned to a particular area

explanation.surface: A nomadic tribe is allocated land away from the east of a Turkish port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wandering' rearranges TRIBE to TREBI; ZONED loses its E to give ZOND.
explanation.definitionFit: Trebizond, now Trabzon, is a historic port city on Turkey's Black Sea coast.

clue.text: Sound disapproving of former ruler, in brief

definitions.meaning: a click of the tongue expressing disapproval
short for Tutankhamun, the boy pharaoh of ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: Making a disapproving noise about an old king.
explanation.definitionFit: Tut is a noise of reproof, and King Tut is a nickname for Tutankhamun.

clue.text: Famous rider's heading off, having time to get on mount

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Paul Revere made a famous midnight ride in 1775 to warn of British troops

explanation.surface: A celebrated horseman sets off and finds time to climb onto his horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' looks like a horse but is a mountain; Paul Revere is the American patriot of the midnight ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the world's highest mountain, and mount is a standard word for a mountain.

clue.text: Believe America's power is in clutches of fanatical group

indicators.note: in clutches of means held tight inside, so the pieces are contained

parts.note: a sect is a group with extreme beliefs
US is the United States, America
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: America's might is held by a group of zealots, one supposes.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect something is to think it probably true, so it means to believe.
